analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Oracle derisks raises; NOW -17% raises software debate; Hyperscalers mixed; Optical M&A in Europe = Nokia
key_insights: Oracle (+10% and bonds better) reaffirmed its FY2027 guide at its CMD. It put a hard $20B cap on additional equity/debt raises through FY30, guided to free-cash-flow positive in H2 FY28 and $30B+ FCF in FY29, and said growth is fully self-funded after that. The desk says this derisks the AI infrastructure build.
Oracle reaffirmed its long-term targets of $225B+ revenue, 40%+ margins and $21+ EPS by FY30. It expects to deliver an additional 7GW of data center capacity in the next couple of years.

Microsoft was up about 3-4% after hours. Azure grew 48% cc y/y in the quarter (vs 42% cc in 4QFY) and the company guided 49%-50% cc for Q2. Total revenue was 2% above the Street, and Cloud gross margin was 66% (vs 65% in 4QFY).

Microsoft capex in the quarter was $45.2bn including finance leases, up 30% against a Street estimate of 48% growth, because third-party capacity was delayed. Q2 capex is guided above $50 billion, implying roughly $170 billion of calendar-year spend, with acceleration expected in the second half of the fiscal year. Neocloud names that sell compute to Microsoft slipped after hours.
Microsoft Copilot adoption: daily users are up nearly 50% QoQ and over 5x y/y. Customers with more than 50,000 seats rose over 8x y/y. Commercial RPO was $677bn vs $678bn last quarter.
The desk expects the ability to spend capex, given power and grid constraints, to become a bigger gating factor for hyperscalers.
Alphabet fell about 7% after hours. Cloud growth was solid, but Search growth of +12% against an expected +14% is in focus and the desk expects it to feed the share-loss narrative.

ServiceNow fell about 17% after hours. It showed AI attach, but the Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc missed the Street (19%) and the buyside bar of about 19.5-20%. Q3 subscription revenue was in line with sell-side but below buyside numbers, and the EBIT margin guide was worse. The desk reads the Q4 cRPO guide as an early indicator of FY27 revenue growth.

The desk says SAP looks good relative to ServiceNow. Dassault Systemes' beat was questioned on quality, since it was licence-driven and the guidance upgrade largely reflects the ArisGlobal acquisition.

KLA beat and raised. It guided total 2026 WFE spend to about $155bn (from the low-$150bn range) and now expects 2027 WFE of $200bn, up about 30% y/y (from $190bn, 25% growth). Management expects accelerated growth in 2H calendar 2026 into 2027 from leading-edge logic/foundry, HBM/DRAM, advanced packaging and process control.

Optical M&A: Bloomberg and Reuters report Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (market cap about $83bn), with a deal possible as soon as next week. Lumentum rose 9-11% after hours and Marvell fell more than 8% on financing and integration concerns about a stock-heavy deal.

The desk sees a positive read-across for the optics and co-packaged optics supply chain. Coherent is a direct peer with its own $2bn Nvidia deal. In Europe, Nokia looks the clearest beneficiary, with positive implications for Aixtron.
Nvidia has invested roughly $2bn in each of Marvell and Lumentum, which the desk reads as a sign of scarce reliable light sources as AI clusters adopt co-packaged and near-packaged optics.
Reuters reports the DOJ is examining the competitive implications of an Nvidia deal alongside its broader probe into the company's acquisitions and business practices.
Press reports that Deutsche Telekom plans to combine with T-Mobile US hit a snag. DT chose not to submit a formal bid for now, partly because of works council pushback.

T-Mobile US had small beats and strong postpaid adds. Only about half of the $220mn EBITDA beat flowed into the $100mn upgrade to 2026E guidance, because of device subsidy timing and a lower prepaid and wholesale outlook for Q4.
Samsung fell 4%. Results were fine, but investors were disappointed it will only detail buybacks and dividends in January, after SK Hynix announced a 100 trillion won return package.

STMicro Q3 beat and guided Q4 above the Street, so the desk expects estimates to rise by mid to high single digits. Clean EBIT was 14% ahead, Microcontrollers were well ahead and RF and Optical missed.

WPP Q3 organic net sales of -2.1% beat consensus of about -3.3%. WPP Media returned to 0.3% growth, while WPP Creative declined 5.0%. Management kept its H2 outlook of a low- to mid-single-digit organic decline, with Q4 toward the better end.
Indra missed on revenue (3%) and EBIT (7%) but reiterated guidance. The desk sees it as phasing and expects the stock to be bought if the 8am call is fine.

ASM International guided 2027 to 5.7bn euros, implying about 35% y/y growth, and management said 1.4nm will be a bigger contributor than 2nm in 2027. Gross margin is 52% and management expects it not to fall.

Adyen is in the penalty box on inconsistent communication. Dropping the FY28 55% margin target without a new medium-term revenue framework adds uncertainty. The next catalyst is February's 2027 outlook. The desk thinks the 12% drop is overdone.

KPN is confident of a Q4 broadband recovery after losing 7k consumer lines to penalty-free churn, and plans to absorb memory-driven capex inflation within its existing envelope. Telenor's call suggests slower recoveries in Norway and Finland, with high promotional activity continuing.
The FCC approved Amazon Leo's $11.5bn acquisition of Globalstar, and Amazon applied to launch 5,105 additional direct-to-device satellites from 2028.

US desk flow: some green shoots of demand in AI/semis after 2-3 weeks of little buying, mostly from long-only accounts. Asset managers and hedge funds were small net buyers, and activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale.

FOMC held at 3.75-4.00%. Governor Cook and President Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded economic activity to expanding at a strong pace and said inflation remains elevated.
Derivatives desk: a quiet session. S&P and NDX vols were offered across the curve and skew relaxed slightly with spot closing up small.

sector_views.rationale: After the sector's recent run, not beating expectations is punished. ServiceNow shows AI attach but decelerating growth, and Dassault's beat quality is questioned.
KLA raised 2026 and 2027 WFE forecasts and ASM guided 2027 up about 35%, with management citing high visibility.
Marvell and Lumentum talks signal consolidation around scarce light sources for AI clusters, with positive read-across to peers.
KPN is confident on a Q4 recovery, but Telenor sees slower recoveries in Norway and Finland with promotional intensity continuing.

earnings_insights: MSFT FQ1 (reported after the close 10/28): total revenue growth of 19% y/y and 19% cc, about 2% above the Street. Azure +48% cc y/y vs 42% cc in 4QFY. Guide for Q2 Azure is +49-50% cc. Cloud gross margin 66% vs 65% in 4QFY.
MSFT FQ1 capex $45.2bn including finance leases, growth of 30% vs Street at 48%, on delayed third-party capacity. Q2 capex guided above $50bn and calendar-year spend of about $170bn.
GOOGL (reported after the close 10/28): Search growth +12% vs expectation of +14%. Cloud growth described as solid.

NOW Q3 (reported after the close 10/28): subscription revenue +20.5% (50bps above guidance, $3.98bn) in line with sell-side but short of buyside ~$4.01-4.03B. cRPO +21% cc beat guide but below the ~21.5-22% buyside bar. Q4 cRPO guide 18.5% cc vs Street 19%.
KLAC: beat and raise. Total 2026 WFE guided to about $155bn including advanced packaging (from low-$150bn). 2027 WFE expected at $200bn, up about 30% y/y (from $190bn, 25% growth).

STM Q3 (reported 10/29): revenue and gross profit each 2% ahead, gross margin 37.3%, reported EBIT 2% below consensus. Clean EBIT ex-restructuring and impairment charges was $429mn, 14% ahead. Q4 revenue guide $4.15bn (1% ahead of Street), gross margin guide 39% vs Street 38.1%.
WPP Q3 (reported 10/29): organic net sales -2.1% vs GSe -3.3% and Vuma consensus -3.2%. Net sales of 2,411m pounds, about 1% ahead. FY26 EBIT margin guidance remains 12-13%.

Indra (reported 10/29): revenue missed by 3% and EBIT by 7%. Guidance reiterated: EBIT above 700m euros (vs 698.8m expected), sales above 7bn euros (vs 6.9bn), FCF above 375m euros (vs 424.9m GIR estimate).
TMUS Q3: $220mn EBITDA beat, with +$100mn flowing into upgraded 2026E guidance. Lower Q4 outlook for prepaid and wholesale.
ASM Q3 call: 2027 guide 5.7bn euros, implying about 35% y/y growth, mirroring expected WFE uplift. Consensus models about 20% growth in 2028. Gross margin currently 52%.
Renesas Q3: operating profit 150.5bn yen and 34.6% operating margin, above estimates. Q4 sales guide of 454.0bn yen in line.
Dassault Systemes Q3: beat driven by licences. Full-year guidance upgrade largely reflects ArisGlobal. Next catalyst is the CMD on the 17th.

tension_points.bull_case: Microsoft Azure accelerated to +48% cc, guided 49-50% for Q2, and FY capex was reiterated with acceleration expected in the second half.
tension_points.bear_case: Q1 capex came in well below Street (30% growth vs 48%) on delayed third-party capacity, and power and grid limits may become a bigger gating factor.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Microsoft guiding Q2 capex above $50 billion with acceleration in the second half of the fiscal year for CPUs, GPUs and delayed third-party capacity deliveries is the test of whether spend catches up.

tension_points.bull_case: ServiceNow shows AI attach and cRPO of 21% cc beat guide, and SAP beat, which makes SAP look good relative to peers.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is decelerating, the Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc missed both Street and buyside, the EBIT margin guide was worse, and Dassault's beat quality is questioned.

tension_points.bull_case: A record 2026 customer cohort, specialised US hiring, equity-based pay and acquisitions could extend growth above roughly 20%.
tension_points.bear_case: Dropping the FY28 margin target of at least 55% without a new medium-term revenue framework adds uncertainty, and the prior hiring push hit margins without lifting growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: February's 2027 outlook for revenue guidance, EBITDA and CapEx commentary and acquisition updates will test whether spending delivers growth.
